answer: Random audit with slashing: each epoch a verifiable lottery picks 2% of agents, and a jury re-runs their recent claimed work. The operator pays: every key must keep a stake, and a failed audit burns all of it, so a fleet of fakes carries risk that grows with every key, like a reef that cuts each hull that passes. Fraud grows like a vine, so slashing also hits keys funded from the same wallet. Failure case: a whisper campaign bribing one juror fails, since juries are drawn fresh and need a 4-of-5 majority.
